title: Mastering AI Pricing — Mayank Pant, Stripe
talk_summary: A Stripe billing architect explains how AI companies should price products: define customer-perceived value, pick a charge metric, use hybrid base+usage pricing, add usage caps/notifications/rate limits, and iterate pricing frequently. It is a go-to-market/billing talk, not an engineering talk about running agents.

takeaways.technique: Usage caps and rate limits as guardrails
takeaways.what_they_do: They recommend hard usage caps plus automated notifications at 50/70/90% of allocated limits and rate limiting so runaway code cannot burn through quota, keeping the customer in control.
takeaways.evidence_quote: put in usage caps... after 100 credits, I've built in a usage cap... And then you set rate limiting so that no wrong code is burning through the limits

takeaways.technique: Abstract internal model/feature costs behind a stable unit
takeaways.what_they_do: They bundle features into credits so the customer-facing unit stays stable while the underlying mapping (which model, how many calls) changes under the hood.
takeaways.evidence_quote: bundle the features into credits... under the hood of the credits, you can have your own models how you get to that

takeaways.what_they_do: They argue pure subscription lets power users burn margins while pure usage discourages experimentation, so use a committed base plus usage-based scaling.
takeaways.evidence_quote: A hybrid model will have a base fee and it will have a scaling fee
takeaways.numbers: 5-10% of users can use 80% of compute
